scope: Galí, Monetary Policy, Inflation, and the Business Cycle (2nd ed.), Chapter 2: A Classical Monetary Model, with Appendix 2.1 and Exercises 2.1-2.9. The household's infinite-horizon problem with transversality; firms and the unique real equilibrium; neutrality and welfare equivalence of policies; price-level determination under exogenous rates (indeterminacy), inflation-based rules (the Taylor principle including phi_pi = 1) and money-supply rules; money in the utility function, separable and nonseparable; the Friedman rule; and the exercises, including an exact lognormal equilibrium on a constructed Gaussian probability space and determinacy with one predetermined variable.
source: Jordi Galí, Monetary Policy, Inflation, and the Business Cycle: An Introduction to the New Keynesian Framework and Its Applications, 2nd ed., Princeton University Press, 2015, Chapter 2, pp. 17-51.
